title: How should you clean your teeth
paragraphs: We all know that cleaning our teeth is important, right? Because, if you don’t clean them and things go wrong, they can cause you a lot of pain and discomfort. We’re taught from a young age how to clean our teeth, but the question is – do we all clean our teeth in the same way? Is there a specific time, technique, or duration you should be incorporating into your dental routine?

When our milk teeth first appear in our infant years, we are shown, often by our parents, how to clean them – a ritual normally accompanied by some kind of catchy song. As we mature, our baby teeth drop out, replaced by adult teeth. And soon it’s from trips to the dentists that we get more advice. And that’s the issue – when trying to discover the best way to brush your teeth, it feels like there are so many different tips and tricks.

University College London (UCL) analysed 66 sources of toothbrushing advice from around the world. The most commonly recommended techniques incorporated circular movements and horizontal brush strokes. However, there were some deviations. The angle of the brush, use of vertical movements and rigorous scrubbing were all variations on brushing advice.

And it seems that not one single technique is the standard method – so, if that’s the case, how do we know if we’re doing it right? Well – there is some standard advice. It seems that brushing for between two to three minutes, two or three times a day, is the best course of action. And if you’re one of these people who think it’s wise to brush straight after sugary foods to prevent decay, think again. Apparently, bacteria weaken the enamel almost immediately upon eating, so it’s wiser to wait for an hour or so before brushing.

So, while there is not one standardised technique, most dentists recommend a combination of horizontal and circular movements, lasting for between two to three minutes, two or three times a day. Do that, and you might not need too many trips to the dentist.

vocabulary.entry: discomfort /dɪsˈkʌmfət/ n. 不适；不舒服
vocabulary.example: The tight shoes caused great discomfort to her feet.
vocabulary.translation: 这双挤脚的鞋让她的脚非常不舒服。

vocabulary.entry: dental routine /ˈdentl ruːˈtiːn/ n. 口腔护理常规
vocabulary.example: A regular dental routine includes brushing and flossing daily.
vocabulary.translation: 常规口腔护理包括每天刷牙和用牙线清洁牙缝。

vocabulary.entry: milk tooth /mɪlk tuːθ/ n. 乳牙
vocabulary.example: A child usually has 20 milk teeth in total.
vocabulary.translation: 儿童通常一共有20颗乳牙。

vocabulary.entry: infant /ˈɪnfənt/ n. 婴儿；幼儿
vocabulary.example: The infant was able to stand up with support at ten months old.
vocabulary.translation: 这个婴儿十个月大时就能扶着东西站起来了。

vocabulary.entry: ritual /ˈrɪtʃuəl/ n. 例行程序；习惯做法
vocabulary.example: The morning ritual of making coffee helps her wake up.
vocabulary.translation: 早上煮咖啡的习惯能帮她清醒过来。

vocabulary.entry: catchy /ˈkætʃi/ adj. （歌曲、曲调）朗朗上口的
vocabulary.example: The song has a catchy melody that everyone can hum.
vocabulary.translation: 这首歌的旋律朗朗上口，每个人都能跟着哼唱。

vocabulary.entry: mature /məˈtʃʊə/ v. 长大成人；成熟
vocabulary.example: He matured a lot after living alone for a year.
vocabulary.translation: 独自生活一年后，他成熟了很多。

vocabulary.entry: adult tooth /ˈædʌlt tuːθ/ n. 恒牙
vocabulary.example: An adult usually has 32 adult teeth if wisdom teeth fully erupt.
vocabulary.translation: 如果智齿完全萌出，成年人通常有32颗恒牙。

vocabulary.entry: tip and trick /tɪp ənd trɪk/ n. 技巧和窍门
vocabulary.example: The book shares useful tips and tricks for home gardening.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书分享了很多家庭园艺的实用技巧和窍门。

vocabulary.entry: incorporate /ɪnˈkɔːpəreɪt/ v. 包含；纳入
vocabulary.example: The new design incorporates several eco-friendly features.
vocabulary.translation: 这款新设计包含了多项环保特性。

vocabulary.entry: circular movement /ˈsɜːkjələ ˈmuːvmənt/ n. 圆周运动；画圈动作
vocabulary.example: The massage involves gentle circular movements on the shoulders.
vocabulary.translation: 这种按摩需要在肩膀上做轻柔的画圈动作。

vocabulary.entry: horizontal brush stroke /ˌhɒrɪˈzɒntl brʌʃ strəʊk/ n. 水平刷动
vocabulary.example: Horizontal brush strokes are suitable for cleaning the front of teeth.
vocabulary.translation: 水平刷动适合清洁牙齿的正面。

vocabulary.entry: deviation /ˌdiːviˈeɪʃn/ n. 偏差；偏离
vocabulary.example: There was a slight deviation from the original plan.
vocabulary.translation: 实际情况与原计划略有偏差。

vocabulary.entry: vertical /ˈvɜːtɪkl/ adj. 垂直的
vocabulary.example: The wall has a vertical crack running from top to bottom.
vocabulary.translation: 这面墙有一道从上到下的垂直裂缝。

vocabulary.entry: rigorous /ˈrɪɡərəs/ adj. 用力的；严格的
vocabulary.example: The rigorous training improved the team's performance greatly.
vocabulary.translation: 高强度的训练大幅提升了球队的表现。

vocabulary.entry: scrub /skrʌb/ v. 用力擦洗
vocabulary.example: She had to scrub the floor to remove the stubborn stains.
vocabulary.translation: 她不得不用力擦洗地板，去除顽固污渍。

vocabulary.entry: variation /ˌveəriˈeɪʃn/ n. 变体；变化形式
vocabulary.example: There are many variations of this traditional dish across the country.
vocabulary.translation: 这道传统菜肴在全国各地有很多不同的做法。

vocabulary.entry: standardised /ˈstændədaɪzd/ adj. 标准化的
vocabulary.example: The company has a standardised process for quality control.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司有一套标准化的质量控制流程。

vocabulary.entry: course of action /kɔːs ɒv ˈækʃn/ n. 行动方案；做法
vocabulary.example: We need to discuss the best course of action to solve the problem.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要讨论解决这个问题的最佳方案。

vocabulary.entry: sugary /ˈʃʊɡəri/ adj. 含糖的；甜的
vocabulary.example: Eating too many sugary snacks is bad for your teeth.
vocabulary.translation: 吃太多含糖零食对牙齿不好。

vocabulary.entry: decay /dɪˈkeɪ/ n. 蛀牙；腐烂
vocabulary.example: Poor oral hygiene can lead to tooth decay.
vocabulary.translation: 口腔卫生不佳会导致蛀牙。

vocabulary.entry: bacteria /bækˈtɪəriə/ n. 细菌（单数形式：bacterium）
vocabulary.example: Washing hands regularly can kill harmful bacteria.
vocabulary.translation: 勤洗手可以杀死有害细菌。

vocabulary.entry: weaken /ˈwiːkən/ v. 削弱；使变弱
vocabulary.example: Lack of exercise can weaken your immune system.
vocabulary.translation: 缺乏运动会削弱你的免疫系统。

vocabulary.entry: enamel /ɪˈnæml/ n. 牙釉质
vocabulary.example: Tooth enamel is the hardest substance in the human body.
vocabulary.translation: 牙釉质是人体中最坚硬的物质。

vocabulary.entry: combination /ˌkɒmbɪˈneɪʃn/ n. 结合；组合
vocabulary.example: The combination of honey and lemon is good for sore throats.
vocabulary.translation: 蜂蜜和柠檬搭配对缓解喉咙痛有好处。

sentences.english: We all know that cleaning our teeth is important, right?
sentences.chinese: 我们都知道刷牙很重要，对吧？

sentences.english: Because, if you don’t clean them and things go wrong, they can cause you a lot of pain and discomfort.
sentences.chinese: 因为如果不刷牙，牙齿出了问题，会给你带来极大的疼痛和不适。

sentences.english: We’re taught from a young age how to clean our teeth, but the question is – do we all clean our teeth in the same way?
sentences.chinese: 我们从小就被教导如何刷牙，但问题是——每个人的刷牙方式都一样吗？

sentences.english: Is there a specific time, technique, or duration you should be incorporating into your dental routine?
sentences.chinese: 在日常口腔护理中，是否需要遵循特定的时间、方法或是时长呢？

sentences.english: When our milk teeth first appear in our infant years, we are shown, often by our parents, how to clean them – a ritual normally accompanied by some kind of catchy song.
sentences.chinese: 婴幼儿时期，乳牙刚长出来时，通常是父母手把手教我们刷牙——这个过程还常常伴着一首朗朗上口的儿歌。

sentences.english: As we mature, our baby teeth drop out, replaced by adult teeth.
sentences.chinese: 随着我们长大成人，乳牙脱落，恒牙取而代之。

sentences.english: And soon it’s from trips to the dentists that we get more advice.
sentences.chinese: 之后，我们从牙医那里得到更多关于刷牙的建议。

sentences.english: And that’s the issue – when trying to discover the best way to brush your teeth, it feels like there are so many different tips and tricks.
sentences.chinese: 但问题也随之而来：当我们想找到最佳刷牙方式时，总会发现各种各样的技巧和窍门。

sentences.english: University College London (UCL) analysed 66 sources of toothbrushing advice from around the world.
sentences.chinese: 伦敦大学学院分析了来自全球的66份刷牙建议资料。

sentences.english: The most commonly recommended techniques incorporated circular movements and horizontal brush strokes.
sentences.chinese: 其中最常被推荐的刷牙方式是画圈和水平横刷。

sentences.english: However, there were some deviations. The angle of the brush, use of vertical movements and rigorous scrubbing were all variations on brushing advice.
sentences.chinese: 不过，也存在一些不同的说法，牙刷的倾斜角度、竖刷的方式以及用力刷洗，这些都是刷牙建议中的不同版本。

sentences.english: And it seems that not one single technique is the standard method – so, if that’s the case, how do we know if we’re doing it right?
sentences.chinese: 看起来并没有哪一种方法是唯一的标准方式——既然如此，我们怎么判断自己的刷牙方式是否正确呢？

sentences.english: Well – there is some standard advice.
sentences.chinese: 其实还是有一些标准建议的。

sentences.english: It seems that brushing for between two to three minutes, two or three times a day, is the best course of action.
sentences.chinese: 每天刷牙两到三次，每次持续两到三分钟，这种做法是最稳妥的。

sentences.english: And if you’re one of these people who think it’s wise to brush straight after sugary foods to prevent decay, think again.
sentences.chinese: 如果你觉得吃完甜食后立刻刷牙能预防蛀牙，那可就错了。

sentences.english: Apparently, bacteria weaken the enamel almost immediately upon eating, so it’s wiser to wait for an hour or so before brushing.
sentences.chinese: 很明显，吃完东西后，口腔内的细菌会迅速侵蚀牙釉质，所以最好等一个小时左右再刷牙。

sentences.english: So, while there is not one standardised technique, most dentists recommend a combination of horizontal and circular movements, lasting for between two to three minutes, two or three times a day.
sentences.chinese: 因此，尽管没有统一的标准刷牙方法，但大多数牙医都建议结合水平横刷和画圈刷的方式，每天刷两到三次，每次两到三分钟。

sentences.english: Do that, and you might not need too many trips to the dentist.
sentences.chinese: 坚持这样做，你去看牙医的次数或许就能少很多了。
